This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

3. This Writ Petition has been filed by the Authorized Officer of the Bank Petitioner for a direction to the Opposite Party No.1 to disburse the withheld amount of Rs.92,98,156/- in favour of the Bank out of the total awarded amount of Rs.2,06,81,238/- under Section 77 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter '2013 Act') after passing award under Section 30 of the said Act in LA Case No.16/1-252/2018.
4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Opposite Party No. 2 availed Cash Credit loan from the Petitioner Bank in the year 2011 which was enhanced in the year 2017 and ultimately when the loan amount was not repaid, the Bank took steps under the SARFAESI Act, 2002 and also filed OA No.255 of 2020 before the learned DRT, Cuttack which is subjudice.

It is further argued that the land in question was acquired by the Government under the Land Acquisition Act and the Petitioner was issued with a letter by the Land Acquisition Officer, Jharsuguda- Opposite Party No.1 State Bank Of India vs District Magistrate And .... sentences.text: wherein it is indicated that since the account holder (Opposite Party No.2) is one of the land losers due to acquisition of land for construction of NLCIL Talabira Thermal Power Plant (NTTPP), Jharsuguda and as such he is entitled to the compensation under Section 14 of the SARFAESI Act, 2002 and the Bank has already approached the Jharsuguda District Administration under Section 14 of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, the Bank was requested to intimate the outstanding dues inclusive of interest so that the amount can be put on hold and the balance amount can be released in favour of the person concerned.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the Petitioner that in pursuance of such letter, the Bank furnished the account details of the Opposite Party No.2 and it indicated that the outstanding dues against the Opposite Party No.2 was Rs.92,98,156/-.
However, a letter was issued by the Bank vide Annexure-8 to release the amount of Rs.92,98,156/- under Section 77 of the 2013 Act.

The Land Acquisition Officer, Jharsuguda did not take any action rather disbursed amount of Rs.1,13,83,082/- in favour of the other persons and so far as the amount to which the Opposite Party No.2 is entitled to i.e. the Petitioner's share has been withheld which is not proper and justified.
5. Issue notice to the Opposite Parties on the question of admission indicating therein that the matter shall be disposed of at the stage of admission.
Learned counsel for the State accepts notice on behalf of all the Opposite Party No. 1.
One Extra copy of the brief be served on him in course of this week.
Requisites for issuance of notice on the Opposite Parties 2 to 5 by Speed Post with proof of delivery shall be filed by 18.11.2024.
6. Learned counsel for the State shall obtain instructions in this matter by the next date.

7. List this matter in the week commencing from 16.12.2024.
Counter affidavit, if any, be filed in the meantime.
(S. K. Sahoo) Judge (Chittaranjan Dash) Judge AKPradhan/Bijay Date: 13-Nov-2024 16:19:35
